problem_type: Canonical canvas write receipt outruns project persistence
symptom: The real M4 canonical nomi_canvas_plan patch_shots call returned an approved receipt at revision 2 while the durable project.json still reported revision 1, so cold-restart readback could not prove the approved storyboard edit.
direct_cause: executeCanvasWriteTarget committed the proposal receipt and returned the in-memory canvas result while subscribeWorkbenchProjectPersistence held the persistRevision save behind its debounce; immediately after hydration, React could also expose the storyboard surface before its persistence effect installed the active save owner, so the canonical path could mutate before persistActiveWorkbenchProjectNow had a durable owner and the Host surfaced capability_receipt_unresolved.
class_root: The renderer had two unsynchronized readiness boundaries for one mutation: a debounced subscription and an asynchronously installed immediate canonical barrier. Without an owner-readiness handoff before mutation plus cancellation/idle coordination, receipt ordering and no-op decline semantics could be defeated by a missing owner, stale duplicate save, or queued timer.
affected_population: Canonical MCP canvas.write operations, including nomi_canvas_plan patch_shots, issued against an active Electron project
Any storyboard or canvas mutation that commits a receipt while the active project save target is absent, stale, or still queued behind debounce
entry_points: Project Agent Host canvas.write dispatch for nomi_canvas_plan patch_shots
Canonical renderer capability handler used by the public MCP transport
internal_only_reason: Receipt-to-project revision ordering is an internal Nomi renderer/Host persistence contract; no external source defines this local invariant.
invariants: A canonical canvas write does not return its committed result to MCP until the active project save owner is installed and returns a record for the same project with an integer durable revision.
An immediate canonical save cancels queued debounce work and waits for any in-flight save queue to become idle before writing, so one mutation cannot create a second revision later.

A missing, mismatched, failed, or stale save target fails closed as capability_receipt_unresolved or surface_port_stale; the owner-readiness wait is bounded and the caller never receives a success receipt backed only by in-memory state.

The receipt and project persistence remain owned by their existing shared boundaries; the canonical renderer owner provides the ordering barrier rather than a runner sleep or a second persistence implementation.
generality_proof: All public canvas.write calls converge on executeCanonicalCanvasPlanPatch before the main process returns a committed MCP result, and every canonical call first waits for the active save owner then uses the active session single queue handoff. Awaiting persistActiveWorkbenchProjectNow plus cancel-and-idle coordination covers patch_shots and equivalent operations without depending on provider, runner timing, or stored revision.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Sequence canonical renderer mutation, receipt result, and active project persistence; reject an externally visible success when durable save evidence is unavailable.
Cancel queued debounce work, wait for any in-flight queue save to settle, then invoke the single active project save target and return its durable record.
Signal canonical callers after the existing single persistence owner is installed, closing the hydration-to-visible-surface race without a second writer.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The public canvas.write switch is the canonical renderer entry and now crosses the durable save barrier before returning.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: executeCanvasWriteTarget callback for renderer Agent canvas tools
same_class_entry_points.evidence: This callback serves the in-app Agent canvas tool path; its ordinary editing persistence remains debounce-driven and is not the public MCP canonical receipt boundary covered by this fix.

recurrence.reason: The project session intentionally debounces store persistence while proposal receipts are committed synchronously; every canonical caller could expose the same revision inversion whenever its response beats the timer or the save target is unavailable.
same_class_scan: Searched executeCanvasWriteTarget, executeCanonicalCanvasPlanPatch, canvas.write dispatch, applyProposalBatch receipt commit, persistRevision subscribers, and persistActiveWorkbenchProjectNow callers across src/workbench and electron/.
Checked patch_shots, propose_storyboard_plan, arrange_storyboard_to_timeline, staging, and camera operations as equivalent canonical operations sharing the same renderer owner.

prevention.invariant: No canonical MCP canvas write returns a success result until the active project owner is installed and has acknowledged a durable record for the request project.
prevention.failure_mode: Save errors, absent targets, mismatched project ids, invalid revisions, and post-save project supersession return typed failure and do not claim durable success.
prevention.strategy: Place the await at the earliest shared canonical renderer boundary after proposal commit and before the transport response, reusing the existing active save target instead of adding a caller sleep or alternate writer.

legacy_paths.rationale: No alternate persistence implementation is removed; the existing debounced subscription remains for ordinary UI edits and the canonical path now requires its shared active save target.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The ordering invariant is internal renderer persistence ownership and does not depend on a third-party runtime.

migration: No data migration is needed. Existing project records remain readable; future canonical writes establish the durable save barrier before returning receipts.
residual_risks: A canonical call made while project hydration is superseded still fails through the existing surface_port_stale guard; owner readiness is only signaled for the active project and returns unresolved after its bounded wait if no owner is installed.
A receipt committed before a later persistence failure may still require existing recovery classification; this fix fails the response closed but does not roll back an already committed receipt.
The queue handoff waits for existing saves but does not cancel an external writer outside this session owner.
